header.account: A B2B software company's LinkedIn ad account (masked)
header.why_this_window: No spend in the last 30 days. The 24-month monthly check found spend only in 2025-12, 2026-01, so the audit covers those months (under 92 days, so reach works).
header.grade_math: 100 - 1 fail x 12 - 6 warns x 5 = 58; 1 area not graded (no deduction)

scorecard.key_number: 0 conversions from 87 clicks; no conversion recorded in 24 months
scorecard.why: Both campaigns bid for conversions through one Insight Tag URL rule that has never recorded one, so auto-bidding had no signal and no result can be judged.

No target was given and there are no conversions, so no campaign can be tiered on results; feed CTR can't be judged on 25 feed impressions. Campaign structure: pass (one group, one objective, and the two campaigns never ran on the same days).

scorecard.key_number: 99.5% of spend on the Audience Network
scorecard.why: Both campaigns had the Audience Network on and it took almost all delivery; with tracking broken, its value can't be proven either way. Expansion was off on both, so there is no on/off comparison.

scorecard.area: Targeting and who the ads reached
scorecard.key_number: 34% of Campaign A's job function impressions outside its 6 functions
scorecard.why: Campaign B requires titles, skills and interests all together, with 19 titles. Campaign A's seniority held (3% outside) but its function did not; Campaign B's company size was 17% outside (under the 20% line). Rows overlap, so these are shares.

scorecard.key_number: frequency 3.4 in 2 days on Campaign B
scorecard.why: Campaign B reached about 1,400 people and showed each one the ad 3.4 times in 2 days: a small pool for its budget.

Both run maximum delivery, so no bid type comparison is possible. Both flights were under 14 days. Campaign A hit its $15 daily budget on 3 of 6 days (up to 150%), and Campaign B reached 124% of its $35 budget on 1 of its 2 days. The spending group has no total budget, so there is nothing to pace.
Nothing to compare or rotate. Video: 24% view rate and the steepest drop from 75% to 100%. Document, message and event formats not used; thought leader unknown.

scorecard.area: Lead gen forms and lead quality
scorecard.key_number: no lead gen campaign spent; no CRM numbers
scorecard.why: 2 lead forms exist (2 questions each) but no ad on a spending campaign uses one. Lead quality needs lead-to-opportunity numbers from the CRM.

top_fixes.fix: Make the conversion rule record before the next launch
top_fixes.what_to_do: Check the Insight Tag is on the sign-up completion page (Campaign Manager > Insight Tag, or the page source), then change the rule from an exact match to 'starts with' on the page path, and confirm one test conversion shows up before any campaign bids for conversions again. If the test records, the 0 conversions from the window mean nobody who clicked signed up, and the landing page is the next place to look.
top_fixes.how: all spend in the window went to campaigns bidding for this rule's conversions
top_fixes.evidence: get_conversions: 1 rule, EXACT match; CONVERSION pivot over 24 months: 0 rows; 87 clicks, 0 conversions
top_fixes.who: do this on the site and in Campaign Manager (conversion rules are recommendations only in this skill)

top_fixes.fix: Run the relaunch long enough for auto-bidding to settle
top_fixes.what_to_do: Plan each campaign as one flight of at least 14 days, with a daily budget it can spend on every day of it, and judge cost per result only after the first two weeks. Give the group a total budget and a run schedule so pacing can be checked.
top_fixes.how: all spend in the window was on flights under 14 days
top_fixes.evidence: get_campaign_analytics DAILY: Campaign A delivered on 6 days and Campaign B on 2, both on maximum delivery (MAX_CONVERSION); busiest days at 150% and 124% of the daily budget
top_fixes.who: do this in Campaign Manager (budgets and schedules are recommendations only)

top_fixes.fix: Turn the Audience Network off on the relaunch, or split-test it
top_fixes.what_to_do: Relaunch with offsiteDeliveryEnabled false, or run two copies of one campaign with it on and off for two weeks on the same budget, once tracking works.
top_fixes.how: spend on OFFSITE and OFFSITE_IN_STREAM placements across both campaigns
top_fixes.evidence: PLACEMENT_NAME per campaign: 99.5% of spend off LinkedIn; the LinkedIn feed got 25 impressions
top_fixes.who: I can do this now on a campaign you relaunch (update_campaign, after your yes)

top_fixes.fix: Give Campaign B a bigger pool
top_fixes.what_to_do: Drop the requirement that members match titles, skills and interests all at once (keep titles or skills, not both plus interests), and size its daily budget so frequency stays under about 3 a week; the flight length is the pacing fix.
top_fixes.how: Campaign B's spend in the window
top_fixes.evidence: get_campaigns targeting: 19 titles AND 20 skills AND 21 interests; reach 1,400, frequency 3.4 in 2 days
top_fixes.who: do this in Campaign Manager (targeting is a recommendation only)

top_fixes.fix: Check where Campaign A's job function targeting leaks
top_fixes.what_to_do: Compare the functions that got impressions with the ones you sell to. Members can hold more than one position, so part of this is overlap; if one off-target function keeps taking spend without converting once tracking works, exclude it.
top_fixes.how: spend in the job function rows outside the targeted functions (rows overlap, so this is approximate)
top_fixes.evidence: Campaign A job function: 34% of impressions outside 6 targeted values

checks.evidence: both spending campaigns use WEBSITE_CONVERSION for a product sign-up: the high-intent choice, dearer per result than a lead gen form and usually warmer. It fits a sign-up; a content offer would suit a lead gen form or document ad better.
the 2 campaigns in the spending group are both spending campaigns, with one objective (WEBSITE_CONVERSION)

checks.check: Campaigns competing for the same people
checks.evidence: Campaign A delivered 2025-12-18 to 2025-12-24, Campaign B 2026-01-30 to 2026-01-31: 0 shared delivery days, so they never bid against each other. Both require industries and locations, sharing 9 industries and 1 location, but A narrows by seniority and function and B by titles, skills and interests, so overlap can't be measured from the setup.
neither campaign uses a matched or retargeting audience; both are prospecting

proposed_structure: One campaign group for the sign-up goal, with a total budget and a run schedule, so group pacing can be read (the current group has no total budget).

Inside it, one campaign per audience you want to judge apart: Campaign A's seniority and function audience, and Campaign B's title audience once loosened (fix on Campaign B), live on the same dates for at least 14 days so their cost per result can be compared.
Because they would then run together, check Campaign Manager's audience overlap and exclude one from the other if they share most of their pool.
2 to 5 ads per campaign, so a weak ad can be paused without stopping the campaign.
If you add retargeting of site visitors, give it its own campaign and exclude that audience from the prospecting campaigns.
